summary: All six round-1 findings are genuinely resolved: the [hold] line now carries type(exc).__name__ + sanitize_error_message(exc) and is pinned by a mutation-verified test, both doc surfaces are updated and accurate, the bool-guard and constant placement are fixed, and the 'Adding a new engine' checklist now names the rule. The news_bot.py except-binding is correct (exc is referenced only inside the two except blocks; the bare raise re-raises the active exception before the implicit del exc, and no later code in _fallback_publish reads the name). Full suite green: 1643 passed, 456 subtests. One NEW regression came in with the round-3 gemini flip, in a module round 1 did not review: flipping the unknown-4xx default to per-article also flipped 499 (and 409), and 499 CANCELLED is one of only eight 4xx codes Google's own API-errors reference documents for this API — it is the transport twin of the 408 the same change just promoted to outage, so the flip strikes out an article for a class of failure the change exists to hold. Gemini is dormant in production (.env has only OPENROUTER_API_KEY, prod pins LLM_PROVIDER=openrouter), so this blocks nothing today, but it must be closed before gemini is ever enabled.

suggestions.suggestion: STATUS OF ROUND-1 FINDING 3 (gemini): addressed, but the flip overshot. `_CLIENT_OUTAGE_CODES = {401,403,404,429} | {402,407,408}` is right for every code google-genai actually produces EXCEPT 499. Verified against the installed SDK (`/home/vscode/.local/lib/python3.13/site-packages/google/genai/errors.py`): `APIError.raise_for_response` routes every 400<=status<500 to `ClientError` and `.code` is set from the HTTP status, so the classifier sees the raw code; Google's own API-errors reference documents exactly 400, 401, 403, 404, 429, 499, 500, 503 for this API, with 499 = `cancelled` — 'The client cancelled the request before it completed.' Empirically confirmed against real SDK objects: `ClientError(499, ...)` now returns ClaudeTranscreationError, where before the flip it returned ClaudeOutageError. 499 is a transport-level abort — the google-genai twin of `APITimeoutError` (outage on every engine) and of the 408 this very change promoted to outage — yet it now bumps attempt_count and, after 3 occurrences on the same row (attempt_count persists across days), moves the article to `failed_articles`. That is precisely the 2026-07-14 failure shape the change exists to prevent. 409 (ABORTED/ALREADY_EXISTS in Google's gRPC->HTTP mapping) flipped the same way and now diverges from the PRODUCTION engine, where `openai.ConflictError` (409) is classified as an outage — so for 409 the flip moved gemini further from openrouter, not closer. Secondary accuracy point: the flip's rationale, in the code comment and in the new tests, names 413/414/451 as the codes it protects, but none of those appears in Gemini's documented error set, while 499 — the one documented code the flip actually changes — is unaddressed. Fix: `_CLIENT_OUTAGE_CODES = frozenset({401, 403, 404, 429, 499}) | _ACCOUNT_LEVEL_STATUS_CODES` with a one-line comment ('499 is Google's non-standard client-cancelled code — transport, not article; keep it out of the shared set, which is standard-HTTP only'), add a gemini test for 499 -> outage, and either add 409 too or state in the comment why gemini deliberately differs from openrouter on it. Not a production blocker: gemini is dormant (no GEMINI_API_KEY in .env; prod pins LLM_PROVIDER=openrouter), so nothing is currently mis-struck — but this is the one thing that must be closed before gemini is ever selected.
suggestions.benefit: Keeps the flip's win (413-style article-specific codes no longer wedge the queue head) without re-opening the exact hold-vs-strike hole the feature was written to close, and makes the four-engine parity claim now printed in patterns.md true for every code google-genai documents.

suggestions.suggestion: ANSWER TO QUESTION 2 (`getattr(exc, "code", None) or getattr(exc, "status_code", None)`): the falsy-code fallthrough is not reachable, so the flip creates no new hazard there — `ClientError` is only ever constructed via `APIError.raise_error`, which requires `400 <= status_code < 500`, so `.code` is always a truthy int (0/None cannot produce a ClientError at all). But the `or` clause itself is dead in a way that is actively misleading: verified on real SDK objects, `google.genai.errors.ClientError` has NO `.status_code` attribute (only `.code`, `.status`, `.message`, `.details`, `.response`) — which the new comment two lines above correctly states, while the code below it still probes for the attribute. The trap is in the test fixture: `tests/test_gemini_transcreation.py::_make_client_error` builds the error via `__new__` and sets BOTH `err.code` and `err.status_code`. So if a future maintainer 'simplifies' this branch to the shared `_is_account_level_status(exc)` helper — exactly what the `_llm_common` checklist now tells engine authors to do — every gemini test still passes while production classifies every single 4xx as per-article, silently re-creating the 402 strike-out bug for that engine. Fix (two one-liners): drop `or getattr(exc, "status_code", None)` from the classifier, and drop `err.status_code = status_code` from `_make_client_error` so the fixture matches the SDK. Better still, build the fixture through the real constructor — `genai_errors.ClientError(code, {'error': {'code': code, 'message': msg}}, None)` works and populates `.code` the way the SDK does, mirroring the `__new__`->real-constructor upgrade this same diff made for the openai/openrouter fixtures.
suggestions.benefit: Removes a green-test path for a refactor that would break production, and finishes the fixture-realism upgrade the diff already applied to the other two SDK engines.

suggestions.suggestion: STATUS OF ROUND-1 FINDING 1: resolved — the line now logs `type(exc).__name__` + `sanitize_error_message(exc)`, the binding and the bare `raise` are correct, and `tests/test_llm_outage_hold.py::test_hold_logs_the_cause` pins it. One factual slip in the new comment: the misdiagnosis it cites is dated 2026-07-31, but that date is the total prod-host outage (`work/SESSION-2026-07-31.md`: sshd died before greeting, no admin ping arrived at all, no publications) — the generic-ping wording played no part in it, and there was no [E010]/[E011] to misread. The real precedent is 2026-06-10, recorded in project memory `incident_e011_can_be_server_dns` ('Confirmed once: 2026-06-10, test instance ... external checks all green, root cause was server DNS'). Change the date to 2026-06-11 -> 2026-06-10 and, since the source is a memory file rather than a repo document, name it: `(2026-06-10, memory: incident_e011_can_be_server_dns)`. A comment that exists purely to carry institutional memory has to point at the right incident, or the next responder greps the wrong session log and finds nothing about ping wording.
suggestions.benefit: The one breadcrumb the whole finding is about actually leads somewhere; the correct incident (DNS misattributed to Claude) is also the stronger argument for keeping the cause in the line.

suggestions.suggestion: STATUS OF ROUND-1 FINDING 2: resolved — both edits are accurate and land in the right files. Verified claim by claim: patterns.md's 'gemini tests it by `.code`, since google-genai raises one `ClientError` for every 4xx' matches errors.py:183-186; 'the outage pings go quiet after `ping_count >= 3`' matches `outage_state._compute_next_state` (outage_state.py:341-342, returns no pings in steady state); 'increment_attempt is not called ... recap_failures is populated only on the failed branch' matches `_publish_with_retries` returning `('held', None)` (news_bot.py:3675) and news_bot.py:4437-4440. architecture.md's reworded split is correct and correctly delegates the detail to patterns.md. Two gaps worth one sentence each. (1) Neither file records that gemini's unknown-4xx default was FLIPPED on 2026-08-04 — both describe only the end state, so a maintainer reading git-blame on gemini_transcreation.py finds a behaviour change with no entry in the knowledge base; this repo's own convention is an inline dated note (patterns.md already carries '*Corrected 2026-08-03: ...*' two bullets above). (2) architecture.md still opens the Failure model with '(identical whichever engine is selected)', and 409 is now a live counter-example: openai/openrouter hold it (`openai.ConflictError` is in their outage tuple), claude and — since this change — gemini strike it. Soften to 'identical for every code either SDK names; the remaining per-engine differences live in each `_classify_exception`' or fix 409.
suggestions.benefit: Closes the loop between the code change and the two documents that gate future edits to it, and stops the one word ('identical') that a future reader would otherwise trust over the code.

suggestions.suggestion: STATUS OF ROUND-1 FINDINGS 4, 5, 6: all resolved (bool-guard and its false rationale deleted, helper is now plain frozenset membership; checklist updated; constant moved under the `# Constants #` banner). Residual nit in the checklist: step 2's import list names `_is_account_level_status`, but step 3's imperative names `_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_STATUS_CODES` — and gemini, the one engine that cannot use the helper (its SDK exposes `.code`, not `.status_code`), imports the constant instead. An author following step 2 literally imports the helper and then cannot satisfy step 3 if their SDK names the attribute differently. Add the constant to the step-2 list and one clause to step 3: 'use `_is_account_level_status` if the SDK exposes `.status_code`; otherwise test `_ACCOUNT_LEVEL_STATUS_CODES` against whatever attribute it does expose (see gemini_transcreation)'.
suggestions.benefit: Makes the checklist executable for the non-`.status_code` case that already exists in the repo, instead of only for the two SDKs that happen to agree.
